subject: Renewal discussion: SLA uplift + committed throughput & burst capacity
messages:
From: Rachel Kim <rachel.kim@redwood.com>
To: Brian Lopez <brian@helixmedia.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Sean Gallagher <sean.gallagher@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 2 Apr 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Renewal discussion: SLA uplift + committed throughput & burst capacity

Hi Brian —

Hope you had a good week. Our agreement with Helix is coming up for renewal on 2027-05-15 and I wanted to start the discussion around the support and SLA layer you asked about during the Q1 review. You mentioned considering a Premium SLA (24/7 phone support, 15-minute P1 response) and tighter latency SLOs for peak hours to support your new ad-personalization pipelines.

High-level proposal from our side:
- Premium support upgrade (24/7 phone + follow-the-sun rotation)
- Latency SLO: 95th percentile tail <= 120ms for standard generation requests (seq len 512) during business-critical windows (M–F 07:00–19:00 PT)
- Committed throughput: 150M tokens/month baseline with a 20% burst pool available for seasonal spikes; overage pricing tiered thereafter
- SLA credits: sliding credits tied to missed SLOs (examples in attached addendum)

Can you confirm: 1) whether Helix would commit to a 12- or 24-month term, and 2) whether the proposed baseline throughput aligns with your planning for H2? If you prefer, we can run a 30-day ramp test to validate the p95 numbers before committing to a full-term SLA.

I attached your Q1 usage report. Happy to jump on a 30-minute call next week to align.

Thanks,
Rachel
Rachel Kim
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
(rachel.kim@redwood.com)

Attachments: helix_usage_report_q1.pdf (summary CSV + charts)

From: Brian Lopez <brian@helixmedia.com>
To: Rachel Kim <rachel.kim@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 2 Apr 2027 10:38:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Renewal discussion: SLA uplift + committed throughput & burst capacity

Rachel —

Thanks for the clear outline. A few quick points from our side:
- We're leaning toward a 24-month commit if we can secure predictable cost and burst headroom for heavy campaign days (we run lots of launches in Q4).
- 150M tokens/month looks reasonable as a baseline; depending on ad volume growth we may need the 20% burst to be higher (can we get a configurable burst pool that scales with spend?)
- P95 of 120ms is ambitious but attractive; we need to ensure it covers our reranking and short-chat flows as well (will your measurements include those request types?)

I'll loop in procurement next week — copying them as we finalize commercial terms. Also open to a 30-day ramp test.

—Brian
Brian Lopez
Head of Platform Engineering — Helix Media

From: Rachel Kim <rachel.kim@redwood.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Sean Gallagher <sean.gallagher@redwood.com>, Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 5 Apr 2027 08:15:00 -0700
Subject: Fwd: Renewal discussion: SLA uplift + committed throughput & burst capacity

Folks — forwarding Brian's note. He signaled interest in a 24-month term if we can give configurable burst pools and ensure the SLOs also cover reranking/short-chat.

Key asks to consider before we get procurement involved:
1) Can Redwood support request-type aware SLOs (generation vs re-rank vs embeddings) or do we need a single p95 across the board?
2) Configurable burst: propose a spend-tied burst tranche (e.g., +10% burst per additional 50% commit increment) — is that doable from a capacity planning perspective?
3) If we offer a 30-day ramp test, what are the guardrails and metrics we'd commit to measuring?

Marissa — can you draft an addendum that outlines the SLA credit table for missed p95 windows and a burst-sizing approach? Sean — can you confirm ops feasibility for a spend-tied burst pool and whether it requires a Dedicated allocation or can be handled in Hosted with capacity reservations?

Thanks,
Rachel

From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
To: Rachel Kim <rachel.kim@redwood.com>, Sean Gallagher <sean.gallagher@redwood.com>, Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 6 Apr 2027 09:42:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Fwd: Renewal discussion: SLA uplift + committed throughput & burst capacity

Rachel / team —

Draft responses below for Helix: feel free to edit before we share externally.

A) Request-type SLOs: we can define SLOs scoped to request classes. Proposal:
- Gen-standard (seq <=512): p95 <= 120ms (business window)
- Rerank/short-chat (seq <=128): p95 <= 80ms
- Embeddings: median <= 30ms (not covered by p95 SLA initially)

B) Configurable burst pool: we can offer a tiered burst model. Example: baseline commit 150M tokens/month + optional purchase of burst tranches (each tranche = 30M tokens/month at a set rate). Tranches can be added mid-term with a 30-day ramp notice. If Helix prefers spend-tied auto-scaling, ops would need a minimal guaranteed commit (same as baseline) and the rest handled as billed overage with soft reservation windows.

C) 30-day ramp test guardrails:
- Define test traffic lanes (gen, rerank) with representative load; Redwood will run with telemetry enabled and provide daily p95/p99 dashboards.
- Success threshold: p95 <= target SLO 18 of 30 days AND no more than 3 incident-class P1s during the window.
- If success, ramp becomes contractual baseline; if failure, we provide 50% credit on that month's committed spend and a remediation plan.

D) SLA credits: propose sliding credit up to 20% of monthly committed fee for repeated SLO misses; exact language in addendum (attached).

Sean — quick ask: does the tiered burst model require Dedicated? If so, include cost delta for moving to Dedicated vs Hosted reservations.

—Marissa

Attachments: proposed_sla_addendum_v3.docx (SLA credit table + examples)

From: Sean Gallagher <sean.gallagher@redwood.com>
To: Rachel Kim <rachel.kim@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 6 Apr 2027 11:07:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Fwd: Renewal discussion: SLA uplift + committed throughput & burst capacity

Quick ops note —

We can support the tiered burst tranches on Hosted for Helix, but there are operational caveats:
- For predictable low-latency during burst windows we need pre-warmed GPU capacity. That can be achieved via reserved burst tranches (30M token tranches as Marissa suggested) or by moving Helix to a small Dedicated pool with auto-scale headroom.
- Hosted reservations with burst tranches cost less upfront but have slightly higher variance under extreme concurrent spikes; Dedicated gives consistent latency but increases committed cost ~25%.
- Implementation timeline for either approach is ~3–4 weeks for provisioning and test harness.

If Helix signs a 24-month commit, ops prefers a small Dedicated overlay (1–2 GPUs reserved) + hosted burst tranches for elasticity — balances cost and performance.

I'll draft the cost delta and timeline and include it in the addendum for procurement.

—Sean

From: Brian Lopez <brian@helixmedia.com>
To: Rachel Kim <rachel.kim@redwood.com>, Procurement <procurement@helixmedia.com>
Date: Wed, 7 Apr 2027 16:45:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Renewal discussion: SLA uplift + committed throughput & burst capacity

Thanks, all — this is helpful.

Helix is comfortable moving forward with a 24-month term under the following conditions:
1) Contract includes request-type scoped SLOs as drafted (gen p95 120ms, rerank p95 80ms)
2) Baseline 150M tokens/month + ability to purchase burst tranches mid-term — we prefer the option to add automated tranches tied to increased spend but accept manual tranche additions for now
3) Ops to run 30-day ramp test with the shared guardrails and telemetry; success moves us to full term
4) We will issue an initial PO for the first quarter upon receipt of the addendum and final pricing schedule; procurement to follow up with standard PO template.

Please send finalized addendum and DocuSign link and we'll route the PO this week.

Best,
Brian
